seo.title: Cadence documentation — emails, invitations & server flow
seo.description: Cadence documentation: invitation email content, confirmation screens, dynamic variables, accept/decline scenarios, server flow, and authorization rules.
page.title: Documentation — How it works
s1.heading: 1. Flow overview
s1.p1: An appointment is created by a signed-in organizer, then sent to a guest via a unique public link. The guest doesn't need an account: they respond from a public page, and the response instantly appears on the organizer's dashboard.
s1.diagram:
Organizer (signed in)
  └─ creates an appointment  ──▶  appointments (status = pending, invite_token generated)
        ├─ "Send by email"  ──▶  server fn sendInviteEmail  ──▶  Resend
        └─ "Copy link"      ──▶  /invite/<token>

Guest (no account)
  └─ opens /invite/<token>  ──▶  RPC get_invite(_token)   (filtered public read)
        └─ Accept / Decline ──▶  RPC respond_to_invite(_token, _accept, _message)
              └─ status = accepted | declined, responded_at = now()

Organizer
  └─ dashboard: status badge, response date, guest message, stats
s2.heading: 2. Invitation email content
s2.p1_prefix: The email is composed server-side in the
s2.p1_mid1: function and sent via Resend. Sender: value of
s2.list: Appointment title in bold, then date and time slot formatted for the locale.
Location and description, each shown only if filled in.
Green "Confirm or decline" action button pointing to the invite link.
Plain-text link reminder, for mail clients that block buttons.
"Google reviews" block (Business): business name, rating, review link, Maps link.
s2.p3: All dynamic values are HTML-escaped before insertion: nothing an organizer types can inject markup into the email.

vars.guestName: Greeting line "Hi {{guestName}},". Empty if no contact is attached.
vars.title: Email subject "Appointment: {{title}}" and bold title in the body.
vars.dateRange: Formatted per locale: "Tuesday, Aug 12, 3:00 PM → 3:30 PM" (Intl.DateTimeFormat).
vars.location: Line "Location: …". The whole block is omitted if the field is empty.
vars.description: Free-text paragraph shown below the date. Omitted if empty.
vars.inviteLink: "Confirm or decline" button + plain-text link reminder at the bottom of the email (copy/paste).
vars.inviteMessage: Green custom-message box, shown only for a Business organizer.
vars.googleBlock: "Google reviews" block in the email footer and on the invite page, if enabled.

s2.fail.no_email: the contact has no email address. The organizer has to copy the link and send it through another channel.
s2.fail.no_api_key: the sending key isn't configured. The invite link is still returned to the UI for manual copying.
s2.fail.provider_error: the email provider rejected it (invalid address, unverified domain…). The appointment status stays unchanged.
s2.fail.success_suffix: is timestamped: this field feeds the "links sent" tracking in the stats.
s3.heading: 3. Confirmation screens (page /invite/<token>)
s3.p1_prefix: A public page, no authentication required, rendered from the secured
s3.p1_suffix: function, which only returns the fields needed for display.
s3.loading_text: animated skeleton (calendar) while the response hasn't arrived yet.
s3.invalid_text: error message; no information about the organizer or the appointment is disclosed.
s3.pending_text: subject, date and time slot, duration, location, organizer name, personalized message (Business), optional free-text field (500 characters max), then two buttons "Accept" and "Decline".
s3.accepted_text: green "Accepted" badge, on-screen confirmation, reminder of practical details, and Google reviews block if the organizer is on Business.
s3.declined_text: red "Declined" badge, message stating the organizer has been notified; the guest can reopen the link and change their response as long as the appointment isn't cancelled.
s3.cancelled_text: the response buttons no longer have any effect, the displayed status stays "Cancelled".
s3.p2: The guest's free-text message is truncated to 500 characters client-side and 1,000 in the database, then shown to the organizer on the appointment record.
s4.heading: 4. Appointment statuses
s4.table.label: Label

pending.label: Pending
pending.set: On appointment creation (default value in the database).
pending.effect: The link is active, the guest can respond. Counted in "responses expected".

accepted.label: Accepted
accepted.set: The guest clicks "Accept" — calls respond_to_invite(_accept = true).
accepted.effect: responded_at and response_message are filled in; green badge on the dashboard.

declined.label: Declined
declined.effect: Same record as acceptance, red badge. The slot stays visible for follow-up.

cancelled.label: Cancelled
cancelled.effect: The link no longer accepts a response (respond_to_invite only updates other statuses).

s5.heading: 5. Server-side flow
s5.create_text: done by the authenticated client; data isolation is enforced by database access rules.
s5.send_text_suffix: : protected server function. It reloads the appointment filtered on the requester's ID, refuses if the appointment doesn't belong to them, composes the email, calls Resend, then timestamps the send.
s5.get_invite_suffix: : elevated-privilege database function, the only public read path. It only returns display fields, and hides branding information for a non-Business organizer.
s5.respond_suffix: : updates the status, message, and response timestamp. It only acts on the row matching the token and ignores cancelled appointments.
s5.usage_suffix: : returns the plan, this month's usage, and the admin flag for displaying quotas.
s6.heading: 6. Authorization logic
s6.organizer_text: full read/write access to their own contacts and appointments, and only those.
s6.guest_text: no direct access to tables. They can only read an appointment via their token and respond to it. The token is random (36 hex characters) and grants access to nothing else.
s6.roles_text: stored in a dedicated table (user, moderator, admin) and checked server-side; they are never read from the browser to grant a permission.
s6.admin_text: access to the /admin area (all accounts, contacts, and appointments) and exemption from Free-mium plan quotas.
s6.plan_text: tier changes can't be forced from the client; only the Stripe payment flow or an admin can change it.
s6.quotas_text: enforced in the database before every creation — 10/15 (Free-mium), 30/50 (Basic), 50/100 (Standard), 250/500 (Economic) contacts/appointments per calendar month, unlimited on Business and for admins.
s7.heading: 7. Checklist for the editorial team
s7.list: Editing an email text: change the sending function's HTML template, not the invite page.
Editing a confirmation screen: change the public invite page.
Any new variable must come from a field already exposed by the public read function.
Never show data from another appointment or another contact on the public page.
Always test all three states: pending, accepted, declined.
